references.text: Noah is described as a righteous man, blameless among his contemporaries – this is why God chooses him and his family to survive the flood
God establishes His covenant with Noah and commands him to enter the ark with his family, which prepares for the command in 7:1
Noah obeys God's command and enters the ark with his sons, his wife, and his daughters-in-law – the fulfillment of the command in 7:1
The righteous have an eternal foundation – a principle illustrated by Noah's salvation through the flood because of his righteousness
Noah's faith and godliness led him to build the ark and save his family, and by faith he became an heir of the righteousness that comes from faith
Noah is called 'a preacher of righteousness' who was preserved along with seven others when the flood came upon the ungodly
Noah's ark and the eight who were saved through water point back to Noah's righteousness and obedience to God's command
The psalm generalizes the historical principle in 7:1: God's salvation is reserved for the righteous at the time of judgment.
The psalm celebrates the principle unfolding in 7:1: God's righteous judgment and salvation are revealed to the world.
